cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please get a replacement receipt from the magician. I paid him, but you've got his number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask him to put yesterday's date on another one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a duplicate of the original, not a new payment. The treasurer mustn't think we booked him twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He only sends duplicates directly to the treasurer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give her the number and explain what to ask for. Stay copied in; I need the receipt, not a successful introduction.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 hands B a missing-receipt follow-up. A3 corrects B2's proposed new dated document to an original duplicate; A5 supervises the intermediary route and refuses to let mere introduction finish B's responsibility.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's another-one offer creates A3's duplicate distinction. B4 restricts the recipient to the treasurer, which causes A5 to have B explain and remain copied in.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to obtain the requested paperwork and B4 knows a delivery restriction. Both are useful contributions even when A speaks as the only person managing the process correctly.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4's restriction into continuing coordination rather than an excuse to return the task to A.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies the magician, payment and phone number. A3 names the treasurer's potential double-booking inference, and B4 supplies the recipient rule.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's successful-introduction contrast is a pointed direction about completion, though somewhat polished; it is caused by B4's new intermediary.
